shortDescription: Shares of Comcast Corporation NASDAQ:CMCSA fell about 8% on Wednesday, extending their decline to a fourth straight session, after the company said third-quarter broadband subscriber losses are unlikely to improve year over year due to pressure, including rational fiber pricing, at a Goldman Sachs…

children: fell about 8% on Wednesday, extending their decline to a fourth straight session, after the company said third-quarter broadband subscriber losses are unlikely to improve year over year due to pressure, including rational fiber pricing, at a Goldman Sachs conference.
Chief Financial Officer Jason Armstrong said Comcast

expects full-year broadband subscriber losses to improve from a year earlier but does not expect an improvement in the current quarter. Co-CEO Michael Cavanagh said fiber overbuild in Comcast's markets has accelerated to about 4%-5% annually from a historical 2%-3%.

Cavanagh also said softness in Orlando, which began in June, has continued into the current quarter. He attributed the weakness partly to gas prices and airfare, as well as a pull-forward in demand following the strong launch of Epic Universe.
Management described 2026 as an investment year, with spending on customer experience, pricing and packaging, and wireless weighing on EBITDA and broadband ARPU. Comcast
also said share repurchases have paused as it works through its planned separation of its connectivity and technology businesses from NBCUniversal and Sky.

Still, management highlighted longer-term opportunities in wireless and enterprise. More than 70% of customers receiving free wireless lines have converted to paid lines, while the enterprise business is growing at a high single-digit rate.
Shares have fallen about 12.7% YTD, sharply underperforming the broader index, which has risen roughly 12% over the same period.

title: Comcast tumbles after Goldman conference flags broadband pressure
